reference: Dante Alighieri, Inferno XXVIII (Italian), Maometto passage; read at https://it.wikisource.org/wiki/Divina_Commedia/Inferno/Canto_XXVIII (CC BY-SA text)
gist_en: Muhammad appears as a split, opened body in Hell; the canto names no wife, no Aisha and gives no age.
why_excluded: The relevant passage is graphic bodily violence (the exclusion rule); it also contains no wives, no Aisha and no age. Nothing from it is placed in passages.json.

reference: Riccoldo, Confutatio (Latin, 1606 print, Venice: Zannettus), sentence beginning 'Est igitur omnino irrationabile' (boast of sexual vigour and of forty men's strength); the same passage is in the 1550 Basel print
gist_en: Riccoldo calls Muhammad a most carnal and unclean man and says he boasted of sexual strength equal to forty men.
why_excluded: The sentence describes Muhammad's sexual potency in terms the rule excludes (sexually explicit). It names no wife, so it is also outside the Aisha question. Orchestrator may decide whether a summary is acceptable.

reference: Riccoldo, Confutatio (Latin, 1606 print), the Mary story sentence 'Mahometus forte cuiusdam Mariae amore tenebatur' and the following lines on the concubine
gist_en: Muhammad was smitten with a concubine named Mary; his wives were jealous and found him sleeping with her.
why_excluded: Sexual narrative about a concubine (exclusion rule). Only the wives' jealousy sentence was used (passage A8-riccoldo-1606-aiefe-zelotipia). Not quoted.

reference: Pius II (Enea Silvio Piccolomini), Epistola ad Mahumetem (1461 letter), Latin incunable of 1474 (Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale di Firenze, Magl. A.5.40) read through the text layer of the archive.org scan
gist_en: Pius II attacks Muhammad's law for allowing many wives and concubines and sexual indulgence; the letter names no Aisha and gives no age.
why_excluded: Sexual language and a boast of sexual potency in the relevant lines (exclusion rule); text layer only, not checked against the page image; the letter is addressed to Mehmed II and the referent of 'Mahumet' shifts between the sultan and the Prophet, which needs a closer reading before any quotation.

reference: Alonso de Espina, Fortalitium fidei, book on Muhammad (Lyon 1511 print), lines on Muhammad's libido and luxury (OCR)
gist_en: Espina calls Muhammad lustful and says he claimed sexual vigour equal to forty men; no Aisha name was found in the OCR.
why_excluded: Sexual-potency content (exclusion rule). The OCR of this print is too poor to quote safely and the Aisha search was negative only in the OCR; the relevant page was not read as an image. Status: UNVERIFIED for Aisha.

reference: Roman de Mahomet (Alexandre du Pont, 13th century; French verse, ed. Michel 1831), lines on Mahomet's new law: 'Que uns sens hom .x. femmes ait' and 'Et que .x. femmes ait uns hons'; also 'Encore jouene femme sui' spoken by the widow (Khadija)
gist_en: The poem's Mahomet law lets one man have ten wives; the widow who marries Mahomet calls herself still young. Neither names Aisha or gives a child's age.
why_excluded: Generic polygamy in a speech of a character; no Aisha, no age. The 'young' widow is Khadija, not Aisha. Not counted as a criticism of Aisha's age.

reference: Matthew Paris, Chronica majora, vol. 1 (ed. Luard, Rolls Series 1872), Mahumet passage: names the rich widow as 'Cadisan vel Adige filia Husaitae'
gist_en: Matthew Paris calls Muhammad a most wicked magician whose wealthy patroness (Khadija, given as Cadisan or Adige) clung to him; no Aisha and no age.
why_excluded: Names Khadija, not Aisha; no age. Not a passage about Aisha. Recorded so the orchestrator does not mistake the name for Aisha.

reference: Bibliander 1550 print of the Riccoldo/Kydones Confutatio, second copy of the 'Duae autem ex uxoribus Mahometi ... Aiefe' sentence (text layer only; the same sentence also on the 1606 page 49)
gist_en: Same sentence as the 1606 printing: two wives, one named Aiefe, daughter of Empipecer, jealous of Mary.
why_excluded: Duplicate of A8-riccoldo-1606-aiefe-zelotipia (the 1606 page image is the one verified). Not added to passages.json.
